summary: A superconducting qubit integrated with a 16 m aluminum coaxial cable and SQUID-based modulator realizes single-photon quantum dynamics in a synthetic frequency lattice with $\Omega_{\mathrm{fsr}}/2\pi = 7.33$ MHz and mode coherence times $T_1 \sim 29.1$ µs, $T_2 \sim 57.9$ µs. The platform demonstrates quantum random walks, Bloch oscillations with period $T_B = 5$ µs, non-adiabatic unidirectional frequency conversion, band-structure mapping, and synthetic gauge fields via dual-tone driving.
motivation: Single-photon quantum dynamics in synthetic frequency dimensions have been limited in photonic platforms by losses and weak photon detection, motivating exploration of low-loss superconducting cables recently developed for qubit interconnects.
method: A transmon qubit ($\omega_q/2\pi = 4.32$ GHz) couples to cable modes via a gmon tunable coupler (0 to 7.4 MHz) and is used as a single-photon source and detector; a flux-tunable SQUID modulator enables inter-mode hopping with $\sim 30$ addressable modes within the $\sim 230$ MHz bandwidth near mode indices $m \in [576,608]$; microwave drives on the SQUID synthesize programmable couplings with tunable phases creating synthetic gauge flux $\Phi = 2\phi_1 - \phi_2$ per plaquette.
result: Single-site excitations exhibit nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor quantum random walks; Bloch oscillations occur with detuning $\Delta = -0.2$ MHz; wave packets show asymmetric Bloch motion and undergo unidirectional transport via periodic detuning reversal every 2.5 µs; band structures are measured via Fourier-transformed quadrature readout and verify theory; dual-tone driving at phases $\phi_1 = \pi, \phi_2 = \pi$ and $0.5\pi$ produces tunable band asymmetry.
